title: Flat, locally finitely presented, separated, locally quasi-finite morphisms with universally bounded fibres are finite locally free on a finite stratification (Stacks 07RY)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and whose fibres are universally bounded: there is an integer $n\ge0$ such that for every $s\in S$ the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], residue field $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field]) is a finite scheme over $\kappa(s)$, $X_s=\operatorname{Spec}B_s$ with $B_s$ a finite $\kappa(s)$-algebra, of degree $\dim_{\kappa(s)}B_s\le n$ (the integer $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound], Stacks Morphisms, Definition 03J4). Then there exist closed subsets $\emptyset=Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq\cdots\subseteq Z_n=S$ such that, with $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ for $0\le r\le n$ and $S_r=\emptyset$ for $r>n$, the sets $S_r$ are pairwise disjoint with union $S$, and the following universal property holds: for every morphism of schemes $g:T\to S$ and every integer $r\ge0$, the projection $X\times_ST\to T$ is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] if and only if $g(T)\subseteq S_r$ (as sets). (Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RY.)

proof.text: Define delta(s) as the degree of the finite scheme-theoretic fibre. For every bound n, prove by induction that every sublevel set {delta <= r} is closed. For n=0 it is the whole base. For n+1, sublevels above the bound are the whole base; otherwise the maximal-degree claim makes {delta <= n} closed. Give this complement its reduced induced closed subscheme and pull f back to it. Base-change invariance lowers the bound to n. The induction hypothesis gives the desired closed sublevel there; its image under the closed immersion is exactly the sublevel in S. A closed embedding maps closed sets to closed sets.

Put Z(0)=empty and Z(r+1)={delta <= r}. The closedness just proved, elementary order inequalities, and the bound give a monotone closed filtration ending in S. Each successive difference equals {delta=r}; equality of natural numbers proves pairwise disjointness and choosing r=delta(s) proves the union is S.

For the only-if implication, finite local freeness of degree r on the pullback says every fibre has degree r. Fibre-degree invariance implies delta(g(t))=r, so the image lies in the degree-r difference. Conversely an image in this difference makes all finite fibres of the pullback have degree r and hence gives bound r. Apply the maximal-degree claim to that pullback. Its open degree-r locus contains every target point. Finiteness is Zariski local at the target, so the whole pullback is finite. It is already flat and locally of finite presentation by base change; together these give finite local freeness, and the fibre equalities give degree r. This includes an empty base, and r above n forces the image to be empty.

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 07RY (more-morphisms.tex line 12761) and kept; it now names the 03J4 node def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound (added to stmt_deps). Proof in ten steps along the Stacks proof: base change keeps the hypotheses and the fibre degrees (new unsplit nodes lem-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-base-change for 03J5/03J7 and lem-weil-pbc-separated-lqf-base-change for 01KU/01TM); the claim that the maximal-degree locus S_m is open with X over it finite locally free of degree m, via the etale splitting 02LP (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-etale-splits-off-quasi-finite-part), 02KB (the definition of finite locally free here), 04MH (existing lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-locally-constant), the degree count on fibres (W empty, written out by the sheaf axiom), 03WT (existing leaf) and 02VO (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-free-degree-etale-descent, for etale coverings); closedness of Z_r by induction on n on the reduced induced S' (existing nodes). The universal property is proved from the claim applied to the base change X_T -> T (all fibre degrees equal r), instead of Stacks' T_red / universal homeomorphism / 02LS route, which needs no further node. Source slips: Stacks writes 'S minus S_d' for 'S minus S_n', and 'the claim' is stated for the given n but is used, in the converse, for the base change. Tags 07RY, 02LP, 02KB, 04MH, 03J7, 03J5, 02VO, 022C, 03WT, 01KU, 01TM verified in tags/tags. lean.statement: theorem exists_flat_fp_lqf_bounded_stratification {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [Flat f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [IsSeparated f] (h_lqf : IsLocallyQuasiFinite f) (n : ℕ) (hn : BoundsFiberDegrees f n) : ∃ Z : ℕ → Set S, Z 0 = ∅ ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, IsClosed (Z r)) ∧ Monotone Z ∧ Z (n + 1) = Set.univ ∧ Pairwise (fun r t : ℕ => Disjoint (Z (r + 1) \ Z r) (Z (t + 1) \ Z t)) ∧ (⋃ r : ℕ, Z (r + 1) \ Z r) = Set.univ ∧ (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (g : T ⟶ S) (r : ℕ), (pullback.snd f g).IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree r ↔ Set.range g ⊆ Z (r + 1) \ Z r)
